- README.md:358-364 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The copyable `ai-clarify.yml` wrapper example omits the new `ai:operator-step` exclusion from its predicate.
  WHY: The README example no longer matches the canonical predicate, causing the predicate-parity test to fail and giving consumers a wrapper without the new exclusion.
- README.md:336-337 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The prose list of labels excluded from clarification omits `ai:operator-step`.
  WHY: Operators reading the README will not know that issues with this label are excluded; severity disagreement: some reviewers rate this MAJOR or NIT, while others report it as BLOCKER as part of a combined documentation finding.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:339 and 621 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The root guard's assignment-prefix parsing does not recognize `NAME+=` forms, unlike the workflow template copy.
  WHY: An input such as `COUNT+=1 git push` is not recognized as a git subcommand, and the root/template parity tests fail.
- scripts/activation_verify.sh:77-98,197-198,243-249 | severity=critical | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` remains available to the verifier model, whose normalized output is posted to GitHub without secret redaction.
  WHY: Prompt-injected repository content could cause the model to include the inherited key in a verdict field that is posted in a public comment or issue.
- scripts/activation_verify.sh:211-218 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: A failed fix-issue search returns before the operator-step upsert, verdict comment, and Telegram notification are produced.
  WHY: A transient search failure in a secondary deduplication check suppresses the activation run's primary outputs.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:598-615 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: `run_project_activation_verify` removes the worktree but leaves its `${verify_dir}-runtime` directory behind.
  WHY: Each project verification leaves runtime artifacts in `/tmp`, accumulating on persistent runners.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:580 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The activation completion check applies `endswith()` to the raw comment body without trimming trailing whitespace or line endings.
  WHY: A trailing newline, carriage return, or whitespace can bypass the already-verified check and cause repeated Codex runs and duplicate verdict comments.
- scripts/activation_verify.sh:131, 134, and 217 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: Marker checks split bodies on `\n` without removing a trailing carriage return from CRLF line endings.
  WHY: The resulting marker string does not match the exact comparison or anchored regex, preventing recognition of existing activation fixes and potentially causing duplicate issues or re-verification.
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:173-228 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The upsert reconciliation loop re-lists issues immediately after writes without a delay or backoff.
  WHY: Eventual consistency can make verification reads stale, causing retries to create duplicates or exhaust the retry budget.
- scripts/activation_verify.sh:163-172 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: Project-mode activation context omits `changed_files`, although the verifier prompt asks the model to read files touched by the merged change.
  WHY: The model runs without GitHub credentials and therefore lacks the changed-file list needed to identify which files to inspect.
- scripts/activation_verify.sh:140-149 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The PR-files API fallback diffs only `MERGE_SHA^1` to `MERGE_SHA`, which can omit earlier PR commits when the PR was merged by rebase.
  WHY: If the PR-files lookup fails, the verifier receives an incomplete changed-file list and may miss activation gaps in files changed by earlier commits.
- scripts/activation_verify.sh:211-228,249-252 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: Non-idempotent issue and verdict-comment POSTs are retried without reconciling whether GitHub accepted a prior attempt.
  WHY: An ambiguous transport failure after a successful write can cause duplicate issues or comments.
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py:173-195,204-211 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: Read-back verification does not prevent a concurrent writer from overwriting a previously verified tracker-body update.
  WHY: Two writers can PATCH replacements based on the same stale body, so the later write can erase the first writer's entry while both calls return successfully.
- README.md:1145-1148 | severity=critical | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The second copyable `ai-clarify.yml` wrapper example has no `if:` predicate.
  WHY: Consumers copying it do not get the issue-opened/reclarify guard required by the documented wrapper behavior.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
